newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank regulator urges risk control measures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank regulator urges risk control measures.

text.p: Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig on Wednesday issued new guidance for banks on managing the risks from fluctuating interest rates.

"While current risk levels and rate volatilities do not pose serious risk threats to the industry, the increasing sophistication of bank products and activities has expanded the complexity of banks' identifying and managing interest rate risk exposures," Ludwig said.
"This development makes it critical that proper risk management practices be in place, before interest rates become more volatile," he added.

The guidance sets out procedures to be used by bank examiners to evaluate a bank's systems and controls for identifying, measuring, monitoring and controlling exposure to interest rate risk, the agency said.

The issue has become increasingly important in recent years, Ludwig noted. Banks are holding more long-term assets that can be highly sensitive to interest rate moves, particularly mortgage-related loans and securities. Also more banks are writing options in asset, liability and off-balance sheet products, he said.
